isLiveSession.description:
`true` when this is the session the engine is running, so `cursor`,
`historyEpoch` and `liveEntries` are meaningful.

historyEpoch.description:
Present only for the live session. Absent (not `0`) for a saved
transcript, which has no epoch of its own.

cursor.description:
The event cursor this read is exact at — the same fence
`session/getState` reports, read under the same lock. Present only
for the live session.

historyLength.description:
The committed/live fence at the instant of this read. A client
reconstructs the conversation as
`entries[..historyLength] ++ liveEntries` and cannot double-count.

nextIndex.description: Index to pass as the next `sinceIndex`.

truncated.description: `true` when `nextIndex < totalKnown`: there is more to page.

liveEntries.description:
The in-flight turn, projected with the same DTOs. Present only when
`includeLive` was requested, this is the live session, and a turn is
actually running.

presentation.description:
The session's presentation timeline (capability
`presentationTimeline`), read together with this page so the records
and the conversation describe one generation. Absent from engines
without the capability.

entryKind.description:
What this entry actually is. See [`HistoryEntryKind`]: a `user` role
does **not** imply the operator typed anything.

streamingTextIndex.description:
Zero-based index of the text block still receiving assistant deltas.
Live projection only: a running turn can also contain completed
replies, so membership in `liveEntries` alone is not evidence that
its last text block is open. Omitted for closed or committed text.

steeringMessageId.description:
The steering queue id this entry *is*, when the engine delivered a
queued operator message into the running turn.

Live projection only, and never invented: a committed message carries
no queue id, because the queue that minted it is gone by then.

It exists because a client that queued the message holds its own copy
of the text and is told separately — by a `delivered` outcome — that
it reached the model. Without an identity on the projection, that
client cannot tell whether the user block in a conversation it just
re-read *is* the message it is still holding, and has to choose
between showing it twice and not showing it at all. Two messages with
identical text are genuinely two messages, so the text cannot serve as
that identity.

HistoryEntry.description: One role-tagged entry (committed message or in-flight live turn content).

oneOf.description:
A user-role message carrying tool results (and possibly steering text
appended at a delivery boundary). **Never** a new operator prompt.

HistoryEntryKind.description:
What an entry *is*, independent of its wire `role`.

A provider conversation encodes tool results as **user-role** messages.
A client that renders `role == "user"` as "something the operator typed"
therefore invents user prompts that never happened. This discriminator
exists so that mistake is not possible: `role` stays exactly what the
provider protocol says, and `entryKind` says what it means.

omittedReason.description:
`"tooLarge"` (a per-block cap) or `"liveBudgetExceeded"` (the
live-turn retention budget). Present exactly when `text` is
shorter than what was actually said.

fullLength.description:
Byte length of the *original* text before any cap was applied.
Present exactly when `text` was truncated.

oneOf.description:
A reasoning summary — never the opaque provider signature/ciphertext.

`redacted: true` means the provider withheld the text; that is a
policy statement, not a truncation, so it carries no `fullLength`.

inputFullLength.description:
Byte length of the *original* `input_json` before any cap was
applied. Present exactly when `input_json` was truncated, so a
client can say how much it is not seeing instead of assuming the
capped string is the whole input (I8).

turnId.description:
The turn that produced this call, when the stored message
recorded one. Provider `call_id`s are only unique within a
request, so `(turn_id, batch_id, call_id)` is the identity a
client should key on. Omitted — never invented — for transcripts
written before correlation ids existed.

fullLength.description:
Byte length of the *original* `content` before any cap was applied
(I8). Present exactly when `content` was truncated.

oneOf.description: Metadata only — never a base64 payload (secret deny-list).

HistoryBlock.description:
One block of content within a [`HistoryEntry`].

Every variant that can carry capped free text also carries the pair
(`omittedReason`, `fullLength`). They are present **exactly** when the
projection retained less than the original, so a client can always tell a
complete value from a shortened one. Both are omitted — never `null`,
never a fabricated length — when nothing was dropped.

timelineId.description: Stable identity of the timeline; a fork starts a new one.

changeSeq.description: The highest change applied, for ordering live updates after a read.

evictedBeforeSeq.description:
Records with a smaller `positionSeq` were evicted by the retention
bound and are not shown.

durability.description:
`durable` (persisted with the session), `memory` (not yet persisted,
or persistence failed) or `corrupt` (the stored timeline could not be
read; what is shown starts after that point).

PresentationTimeline.description: The records of one session timeline, as of one read.

itemId.description:
Stable identity of the occurrence, the same live, in snapshots and
after a restart. Never derived from a label or from text.

positionSeq.description: Immutable acceptance order within the timeline.

revision.description: Content version; a newer revision replaces an older one in place.

changeSeq.description:
The timeline change that last touched this record (a separate
namespace from `positionSeq`).

occurredAt.description: When the engine accepted it (RFC 3339). Explanatory, never a sort key.

afterEntries.description:
The record follows the first `afterEntries` committed entries of the
session's current conversation (history generation). `0` means before
every entry.

turnId.description:
Set while the turn the record occurred in is still running: the
record belongs at that turn's end, which is resolved when the turn
commits. A record never sits inside a streaming reply.

PresentationAnchor.description: Where a record sits relative to the committed conversation.

oneOf.description: The anchor names entries of the current conversation.
The entries around the anchor were replaced by a compaction summary.
The entries around the anchor were removed by a rewind.
The anchor does not fit the conversation the record was restored with.

PresentationRelation.description: How a record's anchor relates to the conversation as it is now.

taskId.description: The task id as the engine that ran it named it (process-local).

oneOf.description: A main-agent background task reached a terminal state.

messageId.description: The message-bus id of the original publication.

PresentationPayload.description: Bounded, UI-safe content of one record.
